requiredFindings.title: Dependency guard does not bind the root crate's declared feature table
requiredFindings.evidence: D14: adding [features] reviewer-rc = ["serde/rc"] to crates/contracts (inactive in this workspace) passes check_dependencies (dependencyCount 11). A consumer workspace depending on the same crate with features=["reviewer-rc"] resolves serde and serde_core with 'rc' (logs/d14-consumer-metadata.json). The guard binds resolved root features only, not declared feature flags, contrary to the stated 'all root direct declarations/flags including inactive' scope.
requiredFindings.correction: Add subjectDeclaredFeatures: {} to dependency-policy.json. In check(), refuse unless root['features'] equals it exactly. Add fixture-based and real-metadata negative tests for an inactive forwarding feature.

advisories.title: Python flatten alone does not enforce nested $id/$schema identity
advisories.detail: P12: with validate-schemas.cjs neutered and the closure rebound, a nested $id rebasing is accepted, because Python strips $id/$schema without comparing them to the owner. The pinned runtime check covers this today. For defense in depth, refuse nested $id not equal to the owner, and nested $schema not equal to the 2020-12 dialect, in convert().

advisories.title: Report runtime can validate unselected or superseded refs
advisories.detail: P3: an unreferenced $defs entry with a remote ref is ignored at generation (by design) but embedded in report.ts. SchemaRegistry.matches(ref) runs checkEntryPoints for any caller-supplied ref, so unselected or superseded refs (e.g. native2 HelloV3) are reachable from createReportShapeRegistry(). Route to the TS runtime/report owner: restrict matches to the selected entry point set.

advisories.title: Consistent three-way owner rebind remains a review-only control
advisories.detail: P8: registry, options and source-map can be rebound together to a wrong major/owner and --write accepts it. This is acceptable as a visible reviewed diff. Add an explicit --architecture verification (for example in verify_design.py) that source-map architectureSource pins hash-match the architecture checkout, so the source map is checked against the architecture rather than only against itself.

advisories.title: Runtime keyword vocabulary extension is single-source but not semantically closed
advisories.detail: P10: adding prefixItems to schema.ts known (consistent rebind) lets a remote $ref under prefixItems through both the Python and runtime checks, because the runtime visitor does not descend unknown applicators. This is expected for a tooling change; a test asserting that every known applicator keyword is traversed by both visitors would catch it.

advisories.title: Transpiled runtime is written into the generator input directory
advisories.detail: validate-schemas.cjs writes schema-runtime.cjs into inputs/, which is then given to the Rust generator. It is harmless today; a separate scratch directory would keep generator inputs exact.

advisories.title: source-map.json is pinned as generator tooling
advisories.detail: Owner-mapping data now lives in the generator closure file set, so an owner mapping change rebinds the tool closure digest. Consider pinning it from the registry/options side instead, to keep tool identity and data ownership separate.
